summary.text: Mike Levin is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 49th District, first elected in 2018. An environmental attorney before Congress, he now serves on the House Appropriations Committee. His official biography highlights clean energy, veterans' issues and the decommissioning of the San Onofre nuclear plant.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, he was raised in South Orange County and attended Loyola High School in Los Angeles.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Stanford University in 2001, where his official biography says he was student body president, and a J.D. from Duke University School of Law in 2005. He was also a Coro Fellow.
Worked as an attorney specializing in environmental and energy regulatory compliance and governmental affairs, and as an environmental attorney before Congress.
Served as executive director of the Democratic Party of Orange County, served on the board of the Center for Sustainable Energy and, according to his official biography, co-founded Sustain OC.
Won the open 49th District seat in November 2018, defeating Republican Diane Harkey 56.4% to 43.6%, and was re-elected in 2020.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he serves on the House Appropriations Committee, on its Energy and Water Development and Military Construction, Veterans Affairs subcommittees. Earlier he chaired the Veterans' Affairs Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity (2021-2022) and was its ranking member (2023-2024).

His official biography says more than 32 of his bills have been signed into law, including the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2020, and that he founded and co-chairs the Spent Nuclear Fuel Solutions Caucus.

According to his official biography, he is a member of the New Democrat Coalition, the Congressional Progressive Caucus and the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, and lives in San Juan Capistrano with his wife and two children.
